title: Quiche au Roquefort et Noix
subtitle: Roquefort and walnut tart
excerpt: Quiche au Roquefort et noix is a strongly flavoured French tart of Roquefort cheese, walnuts, and eggs in a cream custard. The salt and pungency of the Roquefort dominates the filling. Walnuts add a bitter crunch that balances the richness of the cheese.
sourceNotes: Roquefort is an AOC-protected blue cheese from the Aveyron department in southern France. The combination of blue cheese and walnuts is traditional in the Aveyron and Auvergne regions, where both products are local.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the day before and serve at room temperature. The flavour of Roquefort deepens overnight.

content.text: Roquefort is an intensely salty, pungent blue cheese. This quiche is not for timid palates. The Roquefort carries the flavour and the cream and egg custard merely provides the vehicle. Add no extra salt. The walnuts toast lightly in the oven as the quiche bakes, developing a slightly bitter edge that is exactly right against the cheese.

Roll the pastry to 3 mm thick and line a 23 cm tart tin. Chill 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Blind-bake with baking beans for 15 minutes, remove beans, bake 5 minutes more. Reduce oven to 180°C fan.
Soften the shallots in butter over low heat for 10 minutes until translucent and lightly golden. Spread over the base of the pastry case. Scatter the crumbled Roquefort and walnuts over the top.

Whisk the eggs and double cream together. Season with black pepper only: the Roquefort provides all the salt needed. Pour over the filling. Bake at 180°C fan for 30 to 35 minutes until set with a slight wobble. Rest 10 minutes.

items.cause: Salt was added to the custard in addition to the Roquefort's natural salt
items.fix: Never add salt when Roquefort is in the recipe. Taste the custard before pouring: it should taste pleasantly salty from the cheese alone.

content.text: This quiche is best served warm or at room temperature. A simple rocket salad dressed with walnut oil and lemon juice is the obvious pairing. The bitterness of the rocket echoes the bitterness of the walnuts.
